rationale: A2.4E explicitly requires formulating quadratic and square-root equations using technology from a table. Fidelity V2 uses the secure Data Modeling Lab for both families, requires full fitted coefficients plus a model prediction, and gives more observations than the minimum needed so the task cannot collapse into hand-fitting two or three convenient points.

documents.prompt: Use quadratic regression technology on the full five-row table to formulate the model $y=ax^2+bx+c$. Enter all three regression coefficients, then use that fitted model to predict y when $x={{predictionX}}$.

context.title: Quadratic regression from a table
context.note: Use the regression feature on all five observations. The table has more than the three points minimally needed to determine a quadratic.

solutionReview.headline: Regression technology uses the complete table to formulate the quadratic model.
reasoning: Running quadratic regression on all five rows returns the coefficients a={{a}}, b={{b}}, and c={{c}}.
Evaluating the fitted model at x=3 gives {{pred}}.

attemptFeedback: Use the quadratic-regression command on the full data set rather than fitting only three selected points.
supportHints: Record all three technology outputs a, b, and c before making the prediction.

documents.prompt: A lab records five measurements of a curved response. Use quadratic regression technology to formulate the model $y=ax^2+bx+c$ from the complete table, then interpolate the response at $x=1$.

context.title: Five-measurement response model
context.note: The requested x=1 lies inside the observed x-range but is not one of the measured rows.

solutionReview.headline: Technology formulates the model; interpolation uses that fitted equation inside the observed range.
reasoning: Quadratic regression on all five measurements returns a={{a}}, b={{b}}, c={{c}}.
At x=1 the model predicts {{pred}}, an interpolation because 1 lies inside the measured x-range.

attemptFeedback: Do not label the prediction as extrapolation; x=1 is between observed inputs.
supportHints: Run regression first, then evaluate the fitted model at the fixed target x=1.

documents.prompt: Use the square-root regression technology on the complete five-row table to formulate $y=a\sqrt{x-h}+k$. Enter a, h, and k from the technology fit, then predict y at $x={{predictionX}}$.

context.title: Square-root model fit
context.note: The endpoint is the smallest x-row. The technology uses every later observation to fit the scale parameter a.

solutionReview.headline: Square-root technology identifies the endpoint and fits the scale from the full table.
reasoning: The smallest-x row gives h={{h}} and k={{k}}.
The full-table least-squares fit gives a={{a}}.
The fitted model predicts {{pred}} at x={{x25}}; this is extrapolation beyond the observed x-range.

attemptFeedback: Use the square-root fit on all five rows; do not estimate a from one convenient point.
supportHints: Enter all three parameters a, h, and k exactly as the technology reports them, then use the fixed prediction x-value.

documents.prompt: A sensor response follows a square-root pattern. Use the regression technology on all five observations to formulate $y=a\sqrt{x-h}+k$, then interpolate the response at $x={{predictionX}}$.

context.title: Sensor calibration from a table
context.note: The prediction target lies between observed inputs, so classify the technology-based prediction appropriately.

solutionReview.headline: The fitted square-root equation supports interpolation inside the table's input range.
reasoning: Technology identifies h={{h}}, k={{k}}, and fits a={{a}} from the full table.
At x={{x625}}, the radicand is 6.25 and its square root is 2.5.
The fitted model predicts {{pred}}; the target is inside the observed range.

attemptFeedback: Because the target is between the smallest and largest observed x-values, the prediction is interpolation.
supportHints: Use the square-root fit first; then evaluate the fitted model at the fixed target.

documents.prompt: A student runs quadratic regression on the five-row table but records the x-term coefficient with the wrong sign, claiming $y={{a}}x^2+({{wrongB}})x+({{c}})$. Re-run the regression technology on the full table, repair the model by entering the actual a, b, and c, then use the corrected model to predict y at $x=3$.

context.title: Repair a technology transcription error
context.note: The student's displayed model is not the answer key. Verify the regression output from the full table and correct the sign error.

solutionReview.headline: Technology output must be recorded faithfully before the model is used.
reasoning: Re-running quadratic regression gives b={{b}}, not {{wrongB}}.
Using that corrected model at x=3 gives {{pred}}.

attemptFeedback: The error is in transcribing the technology result, not in the data. Re-run the full regression rather than trying to adjust the prediction only.
supportHints: Compare the sign of the technology's b coefficient with the student's recorded b.
